articles.title: Rochdale AFC Manager Calls for Continued Effort Ahead of Trophy Tie
articles.excerpt: Rochdale AFC's manager emphasises the need for hard work as the team prepares for an upcoming trophy match, highlighting the importance of maintaining focus and determination.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC's manager has stressed the importance of continued effort as the team prepares for their upcoming trophy tie. He highlighted that hard work and focus will be crucial for the team's success in the competition.

As training sessions intensify, the manager expressed confidence in the squad's abilities but reiterated that consistent effort is necessary to achieve their goals.

Fans are encouraged to support the team as they aim for a strong performance in the trophy. The manager believes that with the right mindset and dedication, the team can make a significant impact in the tournament.

Further details regarding the match will be announced in due course, and supporters are advised to stay tuned for updates on the fixture and ticketing information.

articles.title: M62 Westbound Closed Between Junctions 22 and 21 After Multi-Vehicle Collision
articles.excerpt: The M62 westbound remains closed between Junction 22 at Denshaw and Junction 21 at Rochdale following a serious multi-vehicle crash that occurred late on Saturday night.
articles.content_html:
The M62 westbound carriageway is closed between Junction 22 (Denshaw) and Junction 21 (Rochdale) following a serious multi-vehicle collision that took place shortly before 11 pm on Saturday, October 10. Emergency services, including Greater Manchester Police and National Highways traffic officers, are currently at the scene managing the incident.

As of 6:30 am on Sunday, October 11, the westbound carriageway remains fully closed. Motorists are advised to check for the latest traffic updates and allow extra time for their journeys if travelling through the affected area. National Highways has confirmed that the closure is necessary due to the seriousness of the crash, although further details regarding the vehicles involved and any potential injuries have not yet been released.

Drivers approaching the closure are urged to follow official instructions and temporary road signs, as traffic arrangements may change while emergency services respond to the incident. It is recommended that motorists avoid entering the closed section and instead follow the diversion routes provided by National Highways, which may vary depending on individual locations and destinations.

For those travelling westbound towards Rochdale, it is important to check the official diversion arrangements and monitor surrounding roads for potential congestion before selecting an alternative route. Updates from Greater Manchester Police and National Highways will provide verified information as the situation develops.

articles.title: Rochdale Draw 1-1 with Tranmere to Extend Unbeaten Run in League Two
articles.excerpt: Rochdale's unbeaten streak in League Two continues after a 1-1 draw against Tranmere at Prenton Park, with Dajaune Brown equalising in the second half following an early goal from Tom Conlon.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale extended their unbeaten League Two run to five games with a 1-1 draw against Tranmere Rovers at Prenton Park on Saturday. The match saw Tom Conlon give Tranmere the lead in the 15th minute, capitalising on a defensive error by Rochdale to score from 25 yards into the top-left corner.

Despite Tranmere's early advantage, they failed to capitalise on further opportunities, with Tom Ince missing a close-range chance and Dylan Jones firing wide just before half-time. These missed chances proved costly for the hosts when Rochdale equalised in the 57th minute, as Dajaune Brown tapped in from close range after a cross from Charlie Tasker.

Tranmere sought to regain the lead, with Ince's long-range effort hitting the underside of the bar, but Rochdale held firm to secure a valuable point on the road. The result leaves Tranmere winless in their last five matches, having drawn six times this season.

Looking ahead, Rochdale will aim to build on this result in their upcoming fixtures as they continue their pursuit of a strong finish in League Two. The draw reflects their resilience and ability to compete against challenging opponents.

articles.title: Rochdale Council to Consider Motion to Reassess Climate Targets Amid Cost-of-Living Crisis
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Council will discuss a motion from Cllr John Taylor on 13 October, urging a shift in focus from climate targets to addressing the cost-of-living crisis affecting residents.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Council is set to discuss a motion on 13 October that calls for a reassessment of its climate emergency targets in light of the ongoing cost-of-living crisis. The motion, proposed by Councillor John Taylor, suggests that the council prioritise immediate support for residents over its commitment to environmental goals.

In 2019, the council declared a climate emergency and pledged to achieve carbon neutrality by 2038. However, Cllr Taylor argues that the local impact on carbon reduction has been minimal and that resources could be better allocated to address pressing economic challenges faced by the community.

The council meeting will also include updates on initiatives such as the expansion of the electric vehicle charging network and the Rochdale Town Centre Heat Network, which aims to utilise heat from sewers to reduce energy costs for buildings. The council has received a £1 million grant from the Government to support this project and will soon begin seeking a development partner.

As the council considers this motion, residents may be interested in how these discussions could influence future policies and support measures during the current economic climate.

evidence_sources.captured_text: Council called on to ‘scrap climate targets and focus on cost-of-living crisis’ - Rochdale Times Skip to content LATEST NEWS Council called on to ‘scrap climate targets and focus on cost-of-living crisis’ Rochdale Council is being called on to put helping residents during the cost-of-living crisis ahead of meeting environmental targets. When Rochdale’s full council meets on Thursday, it will consider a motion from Cllr John Taylor calling on the authority to rescind its commitment to climate emergency targets. The meeting will also hear updates on expanding the electric vehicle charging network and the Rochdale Town Centre Heat Network which will see heat from sewers beneath Rochdale will be harnessed to cut energy costs and keep buildings warm. The council has received a £1 million commercialisation grant from Government and will begin a tender for a development partner to take the scheme forward and prepare it for construction. Cllr Taylor’s motion reads: “In 2019 this council, in line with national trends, passed a climate emergency motion and committed resources (financial and human) to achieving carbon neutrality. “A key element of the motion was the inclusion of a Carbon Neutral Target which pledged to make both the council’s operations and the wider borough carbon neutral by 2038. “Since 2019 it has become clear that our local impact on carbon reduction is negligible and it does not represent the most efficient use of our resources. READ MORE: Heat from sewers will keep Rochdale warm in future “Consequently, it is appropriate to review our commitment to carbon neutrality and dispense with our 2019 pledge. “This council recognises the direct impact that the cost-of-living crisis and housing emergency have on many residents, and they must be our strategic priorities alongside the efficient and effective delivery of our core services. Future efforts to achieve carbon neutrality must also be cost neutral. “A local repeal will not override national legislation; the UK remains legally bound by the Climate Change Act to reach net-zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2050. “This is not a withdrawal from environmental action nor a belief that climate change is not a serious issue. It is a recognition of what is within our capacity to change and a renewed focus on deploying our controllable resources.” By rescinding the commitment to all climate emergency targets, Cllr Taylor hopes the council will direct resources to address the cost-of-living crisis and housing emergency. By reviewing all ongoing climate, carbon-neutrality activity, Cllr Taylor wants to stop any programmes that cannot demonstrate a “clear resident benefit, financial saving or statutory requirement”. articles.title: ‘Really nice’: an editor’s visit to the new Starbucks on Whitworth Road
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Daily's editor visited the new Starbucks on Whitworth Road with her little girl and found kind, efficient staff, a fully available menu and a welcome that earned a child's verdict: ‘really nice’.
articles.content_html:
There are plenty of ways to judge a new coffee shop. You can look at the menu, the speed of the service or whether it manages to make a quick stop feel pleasant. But after visiting the new Starbucks on Whitworth Road with my little girl, I found that the most telling review came from her.

“Really nice,” she said of the people working there. Two words, and a rather lovely assessment.

As the editor of Rochdale Daily, I spend a great deal of time looking at what opens, closes and changes across the borough. This time, rather than reporting on a launch, I wanted to experience the place as an ordinary customer — and a parent.

What stood out was the staff. They were kind, welcoming and efficient, handling our visit with the sort of ease that makes all the difference when you have a child alongside you. Good service does not need to be theatrical. Often, it is simply being treated warmly while everything runs as it should.

The full menu was available during our visit, too. There were no disappointing discoveries that something we wanted could not be ordered. It is a simple thing, but it matters: choice is only useful when the items are actually available.

The branch, which opened in August near Rochdale Infirmary and Dunelm, provides both indoor seating and a drive-through. For people visiting the hospital, passing along Whitworth Road or simply looking for a coffee stop, those options are convenient. But convenience alone is not what makes a customer want to return.

Children have an uncomplicated way of measuring an experience. They remember whether somebody was kind. They notice when they are made to feel welcome. My little girl did not care about the branding or the opening ceremony; she cared that the people were, in her words, “really nice”.

This was one family visit, not a claim that every visit will be identical. But the team deserve credit for getting the fundamentals right: kindness, efficiency and a menu we could actually order from.

Sometimes a new business makes its best first impression not through a grand announcement but through the people behind the counter. On our visit to Whitworth Road, Starbucks did exactly that.

Editor’s note: This is a first-hand editorial account of a visit, not a paid advertisement. For the original opening report, see Rochdale Daily’s article, “New Starbucks Drive-Through Opens on Whitworth Road”.

articles.title: Festival of Remembrance to bring borough together at Rochdale Town Hall on October 16
articles.excerpt: Rochdale will come together at Rochdale Town Hall on Friday 16 October for a Festival of Remembrance honouring members of the Armed Forces community.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale will come together at Rochdale Town Hall on Friday 16 October for a Festival of Remembrance honouring members of the Armed Forces community.

The event will feature music performed by military bands, an act of remembrance and historic war stories, alongside an opportunity for people to come together to reflect and reminisce.

The Festival of Remembrance is open to everyone and begins at 7pm.

Tickets are priced at £15 and include a pie and pea supper.

### Tickets and event information

Tickets are available through Rochdale Borough Council's event listing.

The council's listing gives the event date as Friday 16 October, with the programme beginning at 7pm at Rochdale Town Hall.

Rochdale Daily will continue to update this report if further information about the Festival of Remembrance is confirmed ahead of the event.

[Buy tickets and check the latest event information](https://rochdale.gov.uk/events/event/1453/festival-of-remembrance)
